desc: Added 2026-08-10 after the chat-agent notice shipped as a bare console line ('no ACP agent configured … so chat is off'): log the way kolu does — Effect's structured logging throughout the server (levels, spans/annotations, one consistent format, quiet-by-default with a verbosity switch), replacing the ad-hoc options.log/console.log seam. Folded in from the sloppiness audit (2026-08-10), same seam: serve.ts's fault path calls process.exit(1) from a bare .catch, bypassing the scope finalizers the file itself documents as load-bearing (and that path is deliberately untested); listener.ts still renders a raw String(cause) one file from the Cause.pretty helper built to prevent it; OLAI_ALLOWED_ORIGINS is read inline with no named constant and no docs mention, unlike OLAI_DIST_DIR's exemplary pattern.

Two things left rather than moved: the frame cap, now RPC_MAX_FRAME_BYTES inside the primitive with no option to move it, so #71 cannot recur; and the surface runtime's lifetime, which went the OTHER way, into serve.ts, which built it. listener.test.ts retargeted off the number onto the sink (real sockets, asserting on what the logger heard). The park is what proved the fence: shutdown.test.ts caught the primitive's teardown hanging under bun (server.close's callback registered while a socket was open — node never sees it), that diagnosis went into kolu #2144, and the fence passes against the primitive now. DISPATCHED 2026-08-10 → Kolu terminal e500de76 (Claude/Opus); PARKED same day: the primitive's teardown hangs under bun (server.close registered while a socket is open — caught by olai's SIGINT fence), fix folded into the human's in-flight kolu listener-migration PR (kolu #2144); a re-pin past that merge unblocks. PR kolu a serveSurfaceApp primitive owning that sequence; at the next pin bump olai deletes its copy and calls one line. Kolu-side work, zero olai conflict. (Filed 2026-08-10 — the sloppiness audit flagged this as a prose-only 'for now' with no tracking id.)

title: Viewing
desc: Seeing your outlines in the browser, kept current with what is on disk.

title: See your outline
desc:
Shipped as PR #58 (squash ac0cba3). Serve a directory, parse and validate the .jsonl files (format core: unique ids, dangling refs, cycles, stored derived state), render the tree read-only in the browser via a minimal surface view. Visible: your outline in a browser tab — or the validation error, with file:line.
Resolved 2026-08-09: entrypoint is `olai web <dir> [--port] [--host]` (nix-built binary; just serve and nix run wrap it; loopback default); UI is a sidebar of found outlines + one tree per route; mirrors render the target subtree inline, marked (cycle-safe); nodes render title with styled #tags, derived done/doing/open status, date badge, and desc as sanitized markdown; packages/store is born here in load-once form (revision-tagged snapshot, codec seam; watcher/probe arrive with live-updates — see docs/brainstorming/architecture.live-store.md); an invalid set renders an error view listing ALL errors with file:line, grouped by file, cross-file errors in their own section; the tree has client-local collapse/expand; e2e is Cucumber + Playwright in kolu's packages/tests shape, features written fresh for this item (nothing ported from the racket branch); styling is Tailwind v4 exactly as kolu does it (utilities inline; no class-validity scanner — accepted trade-off, decided 2026-08-09). Specs: docs/format.md, docs/architecture.md.

title: Live updates
desc:
Shipped as PR #59 (squash ec5aead). Probe-based staleness over the recursive directory, snapshot stream, error cell. Visible: edit a file or git pull, the page updates without reload; break a file, its outline degrades in place while the rest stays live; a cross-file break keeps last-good and shows the error banner.
Resolved 2026-08-09: error scope is hybrid — a file that fails to decode renders its error in place of that one outline (emanote-style) while other outlines stay live; cross-file validation failures (dangling refs, cycles) hold whole-set last-good with the banner (the codec passes decode failures into validate so the snapshot embeds per-outline failures; store stays generic); deletion is not special (a probe diff — dangling inbound refs are ordinary validation errors, no grace window); the commit()/optimistic-concurrency write gate is deferred to the chat item, where the ops layer is born; the periodic backstop probe stays (~60s) alongside the watcher and refresh(); stamps are mtime+size. This item also closes the see-outline test gap: packages/store gets real unit tests. Design: docs/brainstorming/architecture.live-store.md.

title: Zoom & navigation
desc: Shipped as PR #60 (squash e036504), which also carried two server fixes approved mid-flight: a busy port now falls back to an OS-assigned one with both facts logged, and a listen failure reports as itself (ListenFailed) instead of the [object Object] runtime-fault message. Zoom into any node as its own page at /n/<id> — stable set-unique ids make permalinks free, surviving renames and moves across files — with breadcrumbs that always show the canonical parent chain (stateless, even when you arrived through a mirror) and a per-view done-visibility toggle (client-local cell, like collapse). Resolved 2026-08-09 (see brainstorming doc). Depends only on see-outline's tree — can run in parallel with live-updates. Brainstorming: docs/brainstorming/viewing-web.md.

title: Search & filter #needs-brainstorm
desc: NOT DISPATCHED — blocked on its own brainstorm, not on any dependency. Filter-in-place that keeps ancestors for context (Workflowy-style), including tag-click filtering (resolved 2026-08-09: it lands here, not with navigation), and an operator language over derived state (is:done, date:, has:desc). The operator language is a design of its own — brainstorm before dispatch. Racket parity (2026-08-09 audit): archived nodes are excluded from search results. Brainstorming: docs/brainstorming/viewing-web.md.

title: Documents #racket-parity
desc: Shipped as PR #66 (squash ed3ef7f): every .md is a page at /doc/<path> with its own sidebar section; doc-carrying nodes preview one line and render the document inline when zoomed; document text rides the store snapshot (same codec, same revision — no second read path); /media/* pictures route with a both-ends traversal guard (e2e-tested against ..%2f); GFM footnotes with per-block id minting; rehype-highlight bundled, no CDN (e2e asserts nothing fetched off-server). Decisions recorded in docs/brainstorming/viewing-web.md §Documents. Render the served .md files as documents and link them from nodes' doc fields. Moved out of the old editor-growth bucket — it is viewing, not editing. Racket parity (2026-08-09 audit): relative images served safely (racket's /media/* with restricted extensions), highlighted code fences without a CDN, footnotes. Depends only on see-outline's reader; parallel-safe with everything else in this theme.

title: Journal & calendar #racket-parity
desc:
Shipped as PR #62 (squash ccb77a1), including a scope addition: the shipped roadmap nodes carry date fields stamped with their PR merge instants (local -04:00), so this feature's calendar renders the project's own history. From the racket audit (2026-08-09): a month calendar in the sidebar (day-with-content dots, today ringed, day-being-read filled) plus a /today view. All derived from date fields at view time — no stored year/month hierarchy (rewrite decision 11), no `daily` op.
Resolved 2026-08-09: the calendar aggregates the WHOLE set's dated nodes (any outline — the journal-is-a-query decision realized; no Daily.jsonl filename magic); clicking a day (and /today) opens /d/<date>, a day view listing every node dated that day grouped by outline with ancestors for context; /today with nothing dated today renders an honest empty state (creation arrives with editing ops); the calendar shows the current month with prev/next paging.

From the racket audit (2026-08-09): named palettes selected client-side (racket shipped 15, chalk default with AA contrast), stored in localStorage, applied via data-theme — no server round-trip.

Port those original logo assets verbatim; the connection-health indicator shipped separately with PR #61.

Resolved 2026-08-10 (human): a SINGLE unified tree mixing .jsonl and .md — a folder shows everything it holds, as racket had — replacing the two flat sections.

title: Panel rework: toggleable & resizable
desc: NOT DISPATCHED — ready, no open questions; awaits the word. Filed 2026-08-10 from the human's UI evaluation session; ONE item by decision (human, 2026-08-10), operable prototypes at https://claude.ai/code/artifact/e8b0f5ad-f293-4982-a4cc-470565ab320e (evaluation grounded in master@232e774 + live screenshots; the prototype's pop-out floating chat window was explored and DROPPED — human retracted it 2026-08-10, chat stays a docked panel). Every panel gets exactly TWO states — open, or minimized-with-signal; nothing closes to nowhere (resolved 2026-08-10, human — the prototype's third 'closed' state and the chat × are dropped) — and the reader owns the widths. Desktop, all resolved 2026-08-10 (human, on the Prototype 1 shell): sidebar collapses to a ~3rem ICON RAIL (expand, outlines/calendar/docs icons, live dot — app chrome never disappears) and drag-resizes; chat dock drag-resizes; minimized chat is a pill carrying the LAST agent message, pulsing while a turn runs (replacing the bare >_ agent pill, whose sidebar-footer/corner homes go away); the connection dot JOINS that pill — one bottom-right chrome strip answering 'is the app alive' (connection state + last agent message; interacts with no-lifecycle's indicator, which this subsumes on every screen); keyboard map reserved NOW so keyboard-editing cannot collide: ⌘K palette, ⌘\ sidebar, ⌘J chat. A ⌘K palette is the summon surface: navigation, panel toggles, and a '>' prefix that sends to the agent — this ships the palette SHELL; the palette roadmap item keeps jump-to-node type-ahead and op actions. Mobile mirrors it translated: the capped close-on-any-tap burger sheet becomes a real slide-over drawer with scrim; chat becomes a bottom sheet with half/full snap points; its collapsed form is a strip above the thumb with the last message (this discharges mobile-pwa's owed 'chat full sheet'). All layout state client-local in localStorage like chatOpen — never sent. No open questions remain: dispatchable.

title: Solid utilization: what the client hand-rolls that the framework does better #techdebt
desc:
SHIPPED 2026-08-10 (PR #72): all five seams, one PR, each with a test. (1) <ErrorBoundary> around the shell in main.tsx drawing errors/Fault.tsx — what threw, verbatim, and TWO ways out: a reload (the framework's reloadForUpdate) for a stale bundle, and `/` for a page that is poison, since a fault is usually deterministic for its route and Reload alone would loop. The fallback also LOGS it: a boundary swallows, so without that line the fault reaches no console at all and a browser test meets it as a timeout on a missing element. Documented as a FOURTH error surface beside the three that are about the files. (2) createSelector in Sidebar.tsx (one selector, both lists: what is active is a file) and calendar/Calendar.tsx (the open day; deliberately NOT today, which moves once a day and is meant to redraw the grid). Worth more than the comment claims: `page()` mints a new object every wire frame, so the old form re-ran every row's comparison on every frame from the server, not only on navigation. (3) client/scroll.ts owns every statement that moves the page — top on push, per-entry restore on popstate, and history.scrollRestoration = manual (the browser's restore runs into a page this client has not drawn). The router says only WHICH of the two a navigation gets, because a push and a pop are the one thing it knows that scroll.ts does not. Positions are keyed by an entry key in history.state, read at the moment they are written rather than copied, and recorded AS THE READER SCROLLS because popstate fires after the position it was made from is gone. Unthrottled on purpose: a trailing write lands after the navigation and would record the old page against the new entry. (4) preference.ts grows preferenceChanged + watchPreference — one storage listener feeding the existing theme and chatOpen signals, both started from main.tsx where this client starts everything document-lifetime, and a cleared storage (event.key null) counts as a change rather than as silence. @solid-primitives/storage's makePersisted was evaluated and NOT adopted: <html> is the theme's state and the shell's boot script writes it before any module exists, and this file's degradation contract (storage may throw, the preference stands) is a promise made here rather than trusted to a dependency. (5) clock.ts re-reads on visibilitychange beside the timer, and re-aims the timer from where the clock actually got to — in one place, so the rule the file argues for is written down once. TESTS: unit for thrownText, preferenceChanged and the clock's wake (a fake document + setSystemTime); e2e for the fault card, for scroll on zoom/back (verified to FAIL without the fix — the page stayed at 64px), and for a theme picked in a second tab of the same browser, left open on purpose. SETTLED_SELECTOR now knows three shapes of the app rather than two and world.open() quotes a fault card, so no scenario meets a client fault as a bare timeout again.

Filed 2026-08-10 as the follow-up PR #70 asked for (the client stopped keeping a store above the framework's and adopted @solid-primitives/keyed; this audit hunts the same class — hand-rolled code where a Solid primitive is MORE CORRECT, not dependency swaps). Five verified gaps, each with evidence: (1) NO ErrorBoundary anywhere — the app has three error surfaces for DATA (errors/Page, Banner, Broken) and none for its own code, so a thrown render fault is a dead white tab; #70's RangeError crashed exactly this way. Wrap the shell in <ErrorBoundary> rendering an honest 'this page broke' card with the fault and a reload. (2) The sidebar marks its active entry O(n): Sidebar.tsx:120/149 computes current={props.active === file} per Link, re-diffing every row on each navigation — while Picker.tsx:31 (theming, #69) already established createSelector as the house pattern with the rationale written out. Apply it to both sidebar lists and the calendar's open day (calendar/Day.tsx:108); matters more once sidebar-tree lands and the corpus is the Dropbox port. (3) Navigation ignores scroll: no scrollTo/scrollRestoration outside the chat transcript — router.go() keeps the old scrollTop so zooming from deep in a long outline lands the new page mid-scroll, and back/forward restores nothing the SPA redraw doesn't accidentally keep. Scroll-to-top on push, per-entry restore on popstate; chat/Transcript.tsx's follow-discipline is the house proof this is done deliberately or not at all. (4) Preferences never sync across tabs: preference.ts has no storage-event listener, so a theme picked in one tab leaves a sibling tab stale until reload — against the promise clock.ts argues from ('the one stale thing on the screen'). Either @solid-primitives/storage's makePersisted or one listener in preference.ts feeding the existing signals. (5) clock.ts's midnight setTimeout does not survive suspend/background-throttle: a laptop asleep past midnight wakes showing yesterday's ring until the late timer fires — the file's own doc names this exact promise. Re-read on visibilitychange alongside the timer. Audited and REJECTED, so nobody re-litigates: a router library (routes.ts is five shapes and the hand-rolled pushState router is documented as deliberate), Portal for the fixed panels (no transformed ancestors exist), Suspense (errors-as-data is the design). One PR: the five are independent seams but each is small and they share the review.

title: Notes fold to one line
desc: Shipped as PR #74. Filed 2026-08-10 (human, from a screenshot: ~3 nodes per screen once every desc renders in full). Workflowy's answer, adopted: desc renders as ONE dim truncated plain-text line by default — no markdown blocks in the preview. The full desc renders in exactly two places: the node's own zoomed page (it is the page's subject there), and per-node in-place expansion — click the first line to toggle the body open and shut, client-local and keyed by PLACE like collapse. A per-view density switch beside the done toggle: full / first-line, first-line the default (the first line toggles the body open and shut), the same client-local cell pattern as doneHidden. Same visual grammar as md-docs' one-line doc preview. Pairs with title-markdown; independent and parallel-safe.

title: Agents
desc: Coding agents reading and editing outlines through olai.

title: Chat #racket-parity
desc:
Shipped as PR #63 (squash 66d64ff), the largest PR of the rewrite, through three review rounds plus the human's hands-on rounds: ops layer + store write gate + internal MCP + singleton Claude ACP session with racket session semantics; full-parity panel (in-place streaming, persistent folds, live tool progress, dual-source model, append-log transcript with break markers, slash completion + show-all); busy visibility in three places; mid-turn messages queue; packages/chat extracted from the composition root; the sigint-hang fix with a real-process regression test; the mobile burger (sidebar and chat one tap away on phones). One PR: the chat panel — an ACP session (@agentclientprotocol/sdk) projected into surface events; send, stream, cancel. The ops layer is born here (add, mark, move, archive; fractional-ord insertion; temp-file → re-validate → rename → commit) since chat's agent is the first writer; whole-file agent writes stay rejected. Visible: ask the agent in the web app to check something off and watch the outline update live; a refused write (derived state) shows its unfinished children in chat.
Decided 2026-08-09: the former agent-editing and chat items collapse into this one; MCP tools for external coding agents are punted to their own item. Resolved 2026-08-09: Claude first via a claude-code ACP adapter; the server owns one singleton ACP session (olai is single-user); agent→ops channel is an internal MCP server passed via session/new; ops tool calls auto-approved (permission UI deferred); agent reads via internal MCP query tools only (likely incl. grep), no fs; transcripts persist as Claude Code's own session for the served directory so `claude --resume` works from a terminal; errors are never silently ignored — only a succeeding StaleWrite retry is invisible, every genuine failure renders in chat with structured detail. Resolved 2026-08-09 round two: racket chat semantics adopted wholesale (boot adopts the most-recent session for the cwd via session/list + session/load; picker; foldable tool frames; slash completion; model display; nix-pinned adapter) — full parity in the one PR; query tools are over parsed nodes with file:line, no raw grep. Racket parity to preserve (2026-08-09 audit): session picker (list/switch/new — racket adopted the most-recently-updated session on boot), slash-command completion in the chat input, foldable tool calls in the transcript; write ops auto-commit with racket's message convention (capture:/done:/doing:/move:/archive: TITLE) when the directory is a git work tree, with an opt-out; the archive op rebuilds the ancestor title-chain in Archive.jsonl and references keep resolving after the move. Brainstorming: docs/brainstorming/acp.md.

title: MCP for external agents
desc: Shipped as PR #68 (squash 64455f7), authored by Claude/Opus, twice re-based over master moves (theming #69, set-fat #70) with conflicts resolved by the agent on instruction: the ops layer as a command an agent launches. Punted 2026-08-09: expose the ops layer as MCP tools so a coding agent outside olai (e.g. in a terminal) can edit outlines. Chat's internal agent→ops wiring is expected to produce most of this for free.

title: Create an outline
desc: Agents cannot start a new outline file: add_node's plan refuses any file not already under the served directory, and no create op exists. Ship create_outline(file, seed?): a validated relative .jsonl path (traversal-guarded segment-by-segment like /media/*), refuse an already-existing file, optionally seed one first node (same shape add_node mints), ride the store's temp-file → validate → rename → commit write gate, with the capture:/create: git auto-commit convention when the directory is a work tree. Expose through both faces of the ops layer (MCP tools list and therefore chat). Unit tests on the plan refusals; e2e that a live tab shows the new outline without reload.

title: see references: rendered, and writable over MCP
desc: Shipped as PR #79 (squash c04269c). Filed 2026-08-10 from the leg-pain conversation: `see` is the format's free cross-reference — validated, and today invisible and unwritable by agents. Two halves, one PR: (1) RENDER: a node's see refs draw as links to their targets' /n/<id> pages (target's title as the text), on the zoomed page and on rows carrying them — the see half of edges-ui, moved here; edges-ui keeps blocked-derivation. (2) OPS/MCP: a set_see-shaped op (add/remove see targets on an existing node) through the standard write gate, validation refusing unknown targets with the usual teaching error; MCP read tools (search_nodes, read_subtree) carry see in their output so an agent can traverse references. Backlinks (inbound rendering) remain unfiled — this is the forward direction only.

title: Bugs
desc: Known defects, each carrying its diagnosis; per HACKING.md every fix ships with a test that reproduces it.

title: Live view doesn't work at all — and e2e doesn't catch it
desc:
FIXED via kolu PR #2133 (the store merge stops guessing keys) plus PR #61 (pin bump and the failing-shape e2e scenarios: mid-insert, mid-delete, reorder, poisoning — asserting the id multiset). Observed 2026-08-09 in real use: a write to the served directory never reaches the page without a manual reload, while the e2e liveness suite stays green.
DIAGNOSED 2026-08-09 (Grok; DIAGNOSIS.md in the live-dead worktree). Root cause is UPSTREAM in kolu: @kolu/surface's solid writeWrappedValue merges each stream frame with Solid reconcile(next) under the DEFAULT key 'id' — but olai's outline nodes are Located records ({file,line,node:{id,…}}) with no top-level id, so every element keys as undefined and any membership/order change mis-merges the client store: missing nodes, duplicated nodes, scrambled lines, and a poisoned store that stays wrong for all later frames until reload. Server, watcher, probe, bind and WS frames are all healthy (verified leg by leg; the correct frame reaches the browser). A/B-verified: reconcile(next,{key:null}) or plain replacement fixes mid-insert/mid-delete/reorder.
Why e2e is green: every liveness scenario edits in exactly the shapes keyed-reconcile survives — whole-file rewrites at stable indices and end-of-file appends — never a mid-insert, mid-delete, or reorder, and never an assertion on the full id multiset.
Fix direction: upstream PR to kolu (writeWrappedValue must not assume key 'id' for arbitrary payloads — caller-supplied key or replace policy from the stream definition), plus e2e scenarios that fail today: mid-insert, mid-delete, reorder, mid-insert-then-append poisoning, asserting the id multiset rather than eventual title text.
Upstream fix in flight 2026-08-09: folded into the kolu-side agent's scope (branch surface-typed-lifecycle), pointed at DIAGNOSIS.md. Olai still owes, once the kolu pin moves: the failing-today e2e scenarios and the pin bump.

title: Stale server accepted silently — no connection indicator
desc: Diagnosed 2026-08-09. Surface is designed to address exactly this class of bug and olai doesn't use that part: packages/web/src/client/wire.ts calls connectSurface (the no-lifecycle seam) and keeps only .client, discarding the wire status accessor. A tab wired to a replaced/dead server just sits there looking fine: on reconnect the new process closes it with the stale-tab code, the wire retires by design (stops re-dialing, reports status 'retired'), and nothing in the UI says so. Fix: make full use of the framework — derive createServerLifecycle (or consume the status connectSurface already returns) and render a GREEN CONNECTION INDICATOR in the UI (kolu's header dot is the house pattern), with the retired state auto-reloading or showing 'server restarted — reload'. Regression test (HACKING.md): restart the scenario-owned server under an open page and assert the page recovers; assert the indicator reflects connected/disconnected/retired. Pairs with the connection-health pill under mobile-pwa.

title: The fix in olai
desc: Shipped as PR #61 (squash 46b3a70), reworked onto kolu #2133 before merge: connection indicator (corner dot, green only when live), retired-wire recovery ('server restarted — Reload' via reloadForUpdate), createServerLifecycle over the status accessor (whose projection maps retired to down), an identity.info surface member feeding the pid echo — which the agent proved was previously a dead gate — and same-port server-restart e2e scenarios. Decided 2026-08-09: this PR will also adopt the upstream kolu API from no-lifecycle-upstream once it exists, in the same PR.

title: Upstream: make the framework prevent this #upstream
desc: Shipped as kolu PR #2133: the framework owns the stale-tab handshake end to end (system/identity carries processId, the socket feeds its own echo, rejectStaleProcess deleted), the retired state is a required option on connectSurface (type-level, as preferred), and the store merge stops inferring element keys from field names. The agent was briefed on the three shapes with type-level required, the self-feeding pid echo, and the projectStatus retired→down conflation. What to PR to @kolu/surface / surface-app so a future app cannot silently ship a lifeless wire. To be fleshed out from the PR that comes out of no-lifecycle-fix (decided 2026-08-09). Preference (human, 2026-08-09): type-level is always best — the seam should require a status/onRetired consumer at the type level instead of letting it be discarded. Other shapes on the table: connectSurface defaulting a retired-state handler (reloadForUpdate) unless explicitly overridden; the app shell (surfaceAppLayer) owning a built-in connection indicator. Context: docs/brainstorming/surface-utilization.md.

title: Live update still duplicates rows — one layer above the fixed merge
desc:
FIXED 2026-08-10, shipped as PR #70 (squash 298c30c): the client keeps no store of its own.
DIAGNOSED 2026-08-10, and it is olai's, one layer above kolu's merge exactly as suspected — but a CONTRACT violation rather than a keying accident. App.tsx reconciled the day's groups (key `file`) and the outline's rows (key `key`) into stores of its own, and what it handed `reconcile` was BORROWED: `situate`/`rowsFor` mint fresh wrappers, but the records inside them are the served set's own Located objects (derive.ts, dates.ts), and `reconcile` unwraps proxies and mutates the previous objects transitively. Read two days in turn and the entries inside a group merge POSITIONALLY (a Situated carries no `file`), while the `shows` records either side of that merge do carry one and it matches — so instead of swapping a reference, reconcile copied one node's id/title/date/desc over another node's record, in the live store, which is the set every other page is read from. Those writes then invalidated the very memo they came from (`derived` reads every node), so the effect re-triggered itself until the stack ran out: `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded`, frames alternating runUpdates ⇄ completeUpdates. Observed in the browser on opening a second day; the Dropbox-port sighting above (a node drawn twice, a day missing from the calendar) is the same class. Reproduced headlessly against docs/roadmap.jsonl before any fix — the first navigation never converges.
THE FIX: no store above the framework's. The rows are a memo, a day's groups are read straight off the page model, and identity across frames — the only thing the stores were for — is a KEYING question, answered where the rows are drawn by `<Key>` (@solid-primitives/keyed) on `Row.key` and on `file/id` for a day entry. Nothing in the client writes to what the wire hands it, which is now the rule architecture.md states.
E2E: `Two days, read in turn, each still says what it said` fails on the old client (day 06 lists `pack` twice) and passes on the new one. `An outline that arrives beside the open one leaves it whole` closes the new-files gap this entry named — it is green on the old client too, so that gap was coverage rather than a second bug.

title: Ctrl+C doesn't stop `just run`
desc: Done-marked 2026-08-10 (human-confirmed): the fix and its regression test shipped inside chat's PR #63 (squash 66d64ff) — this stamp carries that merge instant. Observed 2026-08-10 on the chat branch; a second wedged instance (a store-only smoke server from the previous night) suggests it predates chat. Investigation so far: SIGINT is delivered and caught (runMain's handler runs), the listener fully closes (no listening socket, no child processes, no TCP connections remain), yet the process never exits — wedged inside Effect scope teardown after all I/O is gone; repeated Ctrl+C is ignored because the handler already tripped. ROOT CAUSE (fixed in PR #63, with the orchestrator's earlier chat-introduced attribution corrected): NOT chat-specific — master hangs identically whenever a browser tab is connected (the chat agent reproduced it with a master build; the orchestrator's clean master test was an idle server with no tab, the wrong discriminator). server.close waits for every connection, and a tab holds two that never end on their own — the surface websocket and the page's keep-alive — so a server with a tab attached never finished its listener finalizer. Fix: the teardown now terminates websockets and destroys idle keep-alives before close. Regression test packages/server/src/shutdown.test.ts: real child process, real websocket, SIGINT, assert exit within a bound — fails against the old finalizer. Fix must include a regression test: start the real server, SIGINT it, assert exit within a bound.

title: WS frame cap undercuts the framework's #techdebt
desc:
FIXED 2026-08-10, shipped as PR #71 (squash 3822a29): the cap is sourced from the framework — `maxPayload: RPC_MAX_FRAME_BYTES + the ndjson delimiter` (the newline rides the wire but is outside what the decoder measures), so the two layers can no longer disagree whatever either of them is re-pinned to. One correction to the audit's account, measured while fixing it: under bun — what actually runs this server — `maxPayload` was never enforced at all. Bun's built-in `ws` ignores the option and applies its own 16 MiB ceiling, closing 1006 "Received too big message" (16777216 delivered, one byte more killed). So the 8 MiB cap was inert in production and the raw-1009 death was a node host's failure mode; the misconfiguration was real, its symptom was not reachable here. That is why the regression fence (`packages/server/src/listener.test.ts`) pins the NUMBER — it fails against the old 8 MiB and against any future drift — beside an end-to-end test that a 9 MiB frame is carried and answered. Also newly known: while bun's ceiling stands, the framework's handled INBOUND oversize path is unreachable here at all — a frame the decoder would refuse is already past bun's limit, and even one at exactly the cap arrives a delimiter byte over it and dies at 1006 rather than 1009. (Superseded 2026-08-10 by PR #78, which moved the cap inside serveSurfaceApp as an unspellable framework constant — see serve-surface-app.)
Found by the surface-utilization audit (2026-08-09): listener.ts sets ws maxPayload to 8 MiB while @kolu/surface's frameLimit classifies oversize at 16 MiB — an 8–16 MiB frame (a big outline snapshot) dies at the raw ws layer with close 1009, taking the whole socket down, instead of the framework's handled oversize path. Fix: source the cap from the framework's constant, with a test. Audit: docs/brainstorming/surface-utilization.md.

title: Kolu integration: auto-configure its MCP in the ACP chat
desc:
Filed 2026-08-10. If Kolu is running on olai's host, the chat agent's session automatically gets kolu's MCP server — a stdio entry (`command: kolu, args: ["mcp"]`, forwarding `PADI_SOCKET`, per juspay/kolu's own `.mcp.json`) added to `session/new`'s `mcpServers` alongside olai's internal tool server (`mcpServersOf`, packages/chat/src/agent.ts — today it only speaks the http shape; this teaches it stdio).

Resolved 2026-08-10:
- **Detection targets padi, not kolu web.** The web server may live on another machine reaching this host as a remote (the motivating topology: kolu web on pureintent, this host runs only the padi daemon — https://kolu.dev/padi/). "Kolu is running" = the padi daemon is reachable: `$PADI_SOCKET` when olai was launched inside a kolu terminal, else padi's state-root-keyed default socket; plus `kolu` on PATH to spawn the stdio server.
- **Per session/new**: detect fresh each time a chat session is created, not once at boot — padi starting after olai still gets picked up.
- **Automatic, no knob**: no flag/env; a knob can come later if ever wanted.
- **Kolu-specific**: no generic extra-MCP-servers mechanism until a second server shows up.
- **Upstream option** (#upstream): the detection logic can live in Kolu itself — e.g. a cheap "is padi reachable" probe verb, or `kolu mcp` failing fast when no daemon — so olai's side reduces to spawn-and-fall-back rather than reimplementing socket discovery.

Hazard found 2026-08-10 while orchestrating, worth knowing before implementing: `kolu` on PATH is not necessarily the host's kolu. Inside a kolu-spawned terminal the padi daemon prepends its own baked agent-tools bundle, and that bundle's `kolu` was an older build reporting the same version string while missing most verbs — filed as juspay/kolu#2146, fixed by kolu#2147 (the injected binary now resolves to the same build as the host's). The lesson survives the fix: a `kolu` on PATH still SPAWNS when it is the wrong build, so detection should confirm the spawned server answers rather than assume the binary is current. The #upstream option above covers this too.

Refs: https://kolu.dev/mcp/, https://github.com/juspay/kolu/blob/master/.mcp.json

title: Commit changes on purpose, not on every write
desc:
Filed 2026-08-10. Today every op commits itself (packages/ops/src/git.ts), so one train of thought becomes a dozen commits — a roadmap gardening session produced eleven, each with a full node title as its subject line. Replace that with a commit someone asks for.

Design: docs/brainstorming/git-commits.md.

Resolved 2026-08-10:
- **The feature earns its place for ONE reason: an audit trail of what the tool wrote.** Chat auto-approves its ops and there is no web editor yet, so every write olai makes is one the human did not type. Not for history (descs carry their own dates), not for sync (olai never pushes), not for undo (the `undo` item plans real op inverses).
- **Manual, not automatic.** Two doors to the same action: a Commit button in the UI, and a `commit` MCP tool the agent calls when it knows its work is done (and can say why). `--commit=off | manual | auto`, default `manual`; `--no-commit` keeps meaning `off`. Never `--amend`.
- **Derive from git, store nothing** — the same discipline as status and blockedness. `git status --porcelain` names the dirty served files, `git show HEAD:<file>` gives the committed side, the existing codec parses both, and the comparison yields node-level changes. Cost is bounded by what is dirty: a clean directory is one `git status` and no parsing.
- **Never show a text diff.** A .jsonl diff is one enormous line per node. Show it in olai's words — "marked done", "note rewritten", "moved under Agents" — rendered from the changed field set.
- **Who wrote it is intent, not truth**: an in-memory list the ops layer appends to and clears on commit, explicitly allowed to be empty after a restart or wrong for edits made outside olai; the panel then shows changes with no writer beside them. The permanent record is an `X-Olai-Writer: chat-agent | mcp | web` trailer, without which an agent's commits are indistinguishable from the human's.
- **Messages prefixed `olai`**, so `git log --grep '^olai'` is the audit view and `--invert-grep` gives back real history.
- **The repo may be busy**: nothing today checks for a merge, rebase, cherry-pick or detached HEAD before committing — an agent marking a node done mid-conflict can swallow a resolution. Under a button this stops being a guess: check the state, disable, say why. This hole is what decided manual over automatic.
- **One derivation serves two views**: pending is HEAD against the working tree, a past change is a commit against its parent. That yields a Changes view (olai's own commits, newest first) and per-node history via `git log -S'"id":"<id>"'` with no extra bookkeeping.

Open at dispatch: what stops pending changes piling up across days and mixing several agent sessions into one commit (the chrome count is a nag, not a plan); whether the agent's `commit` may sweep up the human's pending edits or only its own; and whether the Changes view sits in the sidebar beside outlines/calendar/docs or is only reached from the chrome pill.

Also fix while here: `set_date` prints as `move:`, which beside real reparenting ops reads as a structural change that never happened.

title: Paste an image into the chat
desc:
Filed 2026-08-10. Paste (and drop, and pick on a phone) an image into the chat composer and have the agent see it. Today the whole chat path is `string` end to end and the composer has no paste handler at all.

**What hardcodes text, layer by layer:** `packages/surface/src/chat.ts` (`send: { input: { text: Schema.String } }`), `packages/chat/src/chat.ts` (`begin(prompt: string)`, queue is `string[]`), `packages/chat/src/agent.ts:115` (`prompt: (text: string)`) and `:549`, where the ACP call is a hardcoded single block `[{ type: "text", text }]`. `ChatEntry` (packages/surface/src/chat.ts) has only `text`, so a transcript row has nowhere to name an attachment. `Composer.tsx` mentions none of paste/clipboard/File/Blob.

Resolved 2026-08-10:
- **The agent receives a PATH, as text.** The prompt carries the tmp path; Claude Code reads the file itself. Kolu's model exactly, and it does not depend on `promptCapabilities.image` — which ACP 1.3 does define (`ContentBlock` has an `image` variant carrying base64 `data` + `mimeType`), and which olai could switch to later without redoing the transport. Inline base64 was rejected for now: the bytes would ride the prompt into the persisted Claude Code session.
- **Bytes land in a TMP dir, not under the served root.** That keeps screenshots out of the store's probe and out of anything `commit-button` would commit. One dir per chat session, removed when the session ends or the server shuts down (the scope finalizer).
- **Transport is CHUNKED over an existing surface procedure**, not a new HTTP route — a procedure inherits the origin gate and session `listener.ts` already enforces for the websocket, where an upload route would need its own.
- **The transcript shows a filename chip.** The tab that pasted previews from the Blob it already has; other tabs and any reload show the chip. `/media/*` cannot help — it is guarded to the served root and the file is in tmp — and a second guarded route was judged not worth a thumbnail.

**Copy kolu's derivation rather than re-deriving it** (packages/padi/src/upload.ts, and `scratch.write` in packages/padi/src/surface.ts, at the pin):
- Two independent numbers. `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` = 50 MiB is a POLICY cap on the file; `UPLOAD_CHUNK_BYTES` = 3 MiB is what one frame carries. Before chunking they were the same number and a 26 MB drop closed the socket with 1009, taking every other subscription on that tab's multiplexed wire down with it.
- 3 MiB is chosen, not rounded: it must be a MULTIPLE OF 3 so base64's 3-bytes-to-4-chars grouping divides exactly and every chunk boundary lands on a 4-character group, which is what lets each chunk decode independently (4 MiB fails this — 1048576 is not divisible by 3). 3 MiB raw is exactly 4 MiB base64; plus a <64 KiB envelope that is 4.06 MiB against the 16 MiB budget, ~3.9x headroom. Base64's alphabet contains nothing JSON escapes, so there is no third expansion inside the JSON string — the one expansion it is tempting to forget, and it is genuinely absent.
- First chunk creates the file (no `appendTo`); each later chunk passes back the path it was returned and appends.
- Three details worth taking with it: ONE policy module consumed by both the client's pre-flight gate and the server's authoritative gate, so the two cannot drift on the rejection threshold; `appendTo` carries no authority, because the server re-derives the scratch dir and refuses any path outside it ("a continuation token that happens to be readable"); the dropped filename is sanitized to a safe basename and collision-suffixed.

Also: a phone has no Ctrl+V, so a file input belongs beside the paste handler (mobile-pwa shipped the viewport work this sits on). Drag-and-drop onto the panel is the same machinery once paste works.

title: A bullet is not a task #needs-brainstorm
desc:
Filed 2026-08-10. Today every node is a task: status is derived as done → doing → **otherwise open** (docs/format.md:62), so `open` is what a node gets for carrying no mark, and there is no way to say "this is only a bullet". `checkbox` (PR #75) made it visible on every row on purpose — "open is a visible EMPTY box, not the absence of one".

Workflowy's model, which we are adopting: a bullet is just a bullet, completion is a flag you apply to some of them, and an unticked bullet is plain text rather than an unfinished task.

**No decision ever defended the current model.** Nothing in docs/ argues that every node should have a status. The rule arrived in ac0cba3 (PR #58, the first rendering PR) as part of the derived-status rule, and racket did the same before it (`checkbox` is tagged #racket-parity). Two things hid it: the only outline olai has ever served is its own roadmap, which really is all tasks, so "everything is open" never looked wrong; and format.md:62 argues carefully about WHERE status lives ("a stored value that currently agrees with the computed one is still a second copy") without ever asking WHETHER every node needs one.

Why it matters now: serving the ported Dropbox notes (see sidebar-tree) renders every paragraph as an unfinished to-do, and `search`'s planned `is:open` operator is useless if it matches the whole corpus.

The defect stated precisely: `open` answers two different questions with one value — "a task nobody has started" and "not a task at all". The same shape the manifest cell exists to fix, where an empty collection could not distinguish "never loaded" from "empty".

Three shapes, cheapest first (the human chose the third; the first is a legitimate first step if the screen should be honest before the format moves):
1. **View-only**: draw the checkbox only where something in the subtree is actually marked. No format change; the model still says everything is open.
2. **Opt in**: a `#todo` tag or field makes a node a task. Clear, but adds a concept and migrates the roadmap.
3. **Drop `open` as the residual**: a node is either marked (`done`/`doing`) or has no status at all. Closest to Workflowy, and the honest fix.

Known cost of (3), not a free lunch: the parent rule needs a second case — "all children done → done" becomes "count only the children that are tasks" — and `blocked` has to say what "not done" means for a bullet that was never a task (probably: a plain bullet never blocks). `edges-ui` has NOT shipped, which is lucky: blocked-derivation can be designed against the new model rather than migrated to it. Also touches the query tools and the done-visibility toggle, which both read `open`.

title: Inline markdown in titles #implementing
desc:
- Kolu terminal: `6498b848` (Grok); reviewer `a53e58e8` (Claude Opus)

- Stage: #awaiting-approval — five MUST-FIX findings, all fixed, re-reviewed and then confirmed a second time against the real `renderTitle`. Green at `439a79b`.

desc:

- PR: #87
- The MUST-FIX was a race that lost the user's work: an in-flight `attach` could resolve into a session that had since been discarded, putting a chip on the new conversation naming a deleted file; the send then failed `claim` while the composer had already cleared the draft. Fixed on both ends — the client captures `session?.id` before attach and bails if it moved (`state.ts:177,186`), and the server runs `attach` under the same `switching` permit as `changeSession` and `discard` (`chat.ts:399,365,446`), so `receive` can no longer interleave with `rm(dir)`.
- Review confirmed the security centre: containment is genuinely re-derived, not path-trusting. The server owns the dir via `mkdtemp` under `realpath(tmpdir())` at 0700, and every `appendTo` and send path goes through `claim` → `realpath` + `startsWith(dir + sep)` + `isFile()`. Planted symlinks, absolute paths and `..` climbs all refused. Kolu's chunk derivation was copied faithfully — 3 MiB (a multiple of 3), 4 MiB base64, 64 KiB envelope, 50 MB cap, frame budget imported from `@kolu/surface/frame-limit` rather than restated.
- **FOR THE HUMAN, residuals not yet ratified:** loading the session you are ALREADY in discards the directory without changing `session.id`, so the client guard cannot see it and a stale chip survives — the server refuses that send safely and nothing is lost, but closing it properly wants a conversation generation on the wire. And restore-on-refusal is skipped when the composer is not empty: if you typed while a send was failing, the refused text and chips stay dropped. Earlier deferrals still open: kolu's chunked-upload transport is copied rather than shared, parallel multi-file upload is unsupported pending an atomic collision-suffix pick, and `appendTo` exposes chunking on the wire.
